In particular, the courses offered in both characteristic and related disciplines allow consolidating the basic competencies of materials engineers on different material classes, their manufacturing processes, advanced and "smart" properties and applications, and enable acquiring interdisciplinary competencies that contribute to consolidating technical preparation and increasing the ability of graduates to interact within different company functions throughout the product design and development phase, as well as in managing its life cycle and defining enabling technologies for production systems. At the second year, students are also offered the possibility to choose between differentiated in-depth curricula that, integrating innovation and entrepreneurial aspects, focus on application contexts of different areas, considered strategic and fully consistent with the overall educational project of the study course. In particular, examples include in-depth studies on manufacturing processes and product development, sustainable use of energy, materials and technologies for biomedical and functional applications, and sustainable materials.
